headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0192 — The PDF changed while SMTO was working on it

html:
SMTO-EXE-0192 — The PDF changed while SMTO was working on it

GUID: 13fb2096-8ece-5953-b536-1cab6066e87f
Slug: pdf-document-stale
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • One of the PDFs SMTO was using changed, moved or was replaced while it was working. To avoid saving a result based on an old version, SMTO didn't save anything. Your PDFs weren't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close the PDF in any other program that might save it, and wait for any cloud sync (such as OneDrive or Dropbox) on that folder to finish. Another program saving or syncing the file changes it while SMTO is working.
  2. Ask SMTO to read the PDF's details again, then do the step again. SMTO needs to start from the current version of every PDF it uses.
  3. If the PDF keeps changing, copy it to a folder that nothing else uses and ask SMTO to work on that copy. A copy nobody else touches stays the same from start to finish.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the new PDF it created.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the PDF's location, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A PDF source's revision, hash or resolved path changed between inspection, worker parsing and the pre-publication recheck, or File revision validation failed, so no output was published.

What this means

  • A source revision/hash or resolved source path changed between inspection, worker parsing and pre-publication rechecks, or File revision validation failed. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • A source revision/hash or resolved source path changed between inspection, worker parsing and pre-publication rechecks, or File revision validation failed.

How to diagnose it

  • Reinspect every original source on the same Gateway and compare revisions, paths and proposed page/object selections.

How to fix it

  • Call pdf.info again for every source to obtain the current revision, stop any process modifying or syncing the files, and rerun the operation with the new expected_revision values; the service rechecks each source's path and SHA-256 before and after staging outputs.
  • Read pdf.info again for every source and make a fresh decision using the returned revision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read pdf.info again for every source and make a fresh decision using the returned revision.

How to verify the fix

  • All reviewed sources remain consistent through publication of the separately created output.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
